title: What If One Software Update Crashed 8.5 Million Computers?

scenes.text: What if one software update grounded planes around the world? In July 2024, one did.
A faulty update from the cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike crashed about 8.5 million Windows computers.
Microsoft said that was less than one percent of all Windows machines. Less than one percent was enough.
Thousands of flights were cancelled worldwide, and Delta was still rescheduling hundreds of flights days later.
Insurers estimated the damage to America's biggest companies at about 5.4 billion dollars.
It wasn't a hack. It was a faulty update, shipped by a company paid to protect those very machines.

description:
What if one software update crashed millions of computers at once?
In July 2024 a faulty CrowdStrike update took down about 8.5 million Windows machines, and insurers put the cost to big US companies near 5.4 billion dollars.
